title: Deal with passing the app flavor to dumpcap in at the lowest layer.
description:
Have init_pipe_args() in capture/capture_sync.c just directly call
application_flavor_name_lower(), so that nobody else dealing with
talking to dumpcap has to care about the app name, and remove the
app_name member from the capture_opts structure, as it has nothing to do
with capturing.

Fixes #21324.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 98899857 - Deal with passing the app flavor to dumpcap in at the lowest layer.
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/25278/diffs?diff_id=1838350113&start_sha=c498469c554245863dd06f0d5a54af4c7db16ab4)

I want to make sure I understand this.  capture/capture_sync.c is part of "capchild" static library that calls application_flavor_name_lower(), but on its own can't link to the implementation of application_flavor_name_lower().  But when Wireshark or Stratoshark are built, they pull in "capchild" static library with the appropriate application_flavor_name_lower() implementation so that this still works with both applications as intended.
I guess I didn't quite understand how capture/capture_sync.c was pulled into the applications, which led to the creation of passing the application name around way more than it needed to be.  Because I thought if the application name wasn't passed around as much, we'd need dumpcap_wireshark and dumpcap_stratoshark.

> capture/capture_sync.c is part of "capchild" static library

...which means that it's linked into a program *only if a function or variable defined in it is called by that program*.

The only sync pipe routines called by dumpcap are the `sync_pipe_write` functions, which are defined in capture/sync_pipe_write.c, which is a *separate* file.

Dumpcap has no need to call any of the routines in capture/capture_sync.c, because those routines are routines that *run dumpcap*, *send messages to dumpcap* and *receive messages from dumpcap*, none of which dumpcap *itself* needs to do.

> I guess I didn't quite understand how capture/capture_sync.c was pulled into the applications

By linking with the capchilb static library and calling routines in capture/capture_sync.c.

Dumpcap, however, is explicitly built from some *source* files in the capture directory, and capture/capture_sync.c is *not* one of those files.

> Because I thought if the application name wasn't passed around as much, we'd need dumpcap_wireshark and dumpcap_stratoshark.

Maybe we should have dumpcap and dumpevents as separate programs; they'd share a bunch of code, but not all of it. See #21334.
